question.text: Vatsalya Charitable Society (child-welfare NPO) received INR 12 lakh of donations during the year where the donors' identities were NOT recorded. Total donations for the year were INR 2 crore. How will the SIA flag this for tax treatment in the pre-engagement note?

answer.text: The entire INR 12 lakh is fully exempt because the NPO is 12AB registered
Anonymous donations above the higher of INR 1 lakh or 5% of total donations are taxed at 30% under Section 115BBI
Anonymous donations are taxed at the marginal slab rate applicable to the donor
Anonymous donations up to 25% of total donations are exempt; balance taxed at 20%

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 115BBI (read with Section 11/13) imposes a flat 30% tax on anonymous donations received by a charitable NPO above the threshold of the HIGHER of INR 1 lakh or 5% of total donations. 5% of INR 2 crore = INR 10 lakh, so the threshold is INR 10 lakh (higher of 1 lakh and 10 lakh). Anonymous donations above INR 10 lakh (i.e., INR 2 lakh of the INR 12 lakh) are taxed at 30%. The chapter explicitly cites the 30% flat rate for anonymous donations. The Trap: Full exemption is wrong — 12AB registration does not protect anonymous donations. Slab-rate taxation of the donor is irrelevant; it's the NPO that is taxed on the receipt. The '25% exempt / 20% balance' option is a fabricated distractor. Cross-Exam Context: XXIV / IFSCA-01 (AML) tests the KYC and source-of-funds angle; XXIII tests the tax leakage angle on the NPO side. X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) may touch 115BBI when advising donors. Assessor's Pro-Tip: As part of SAS-100, walk the donation register for 5-10 sampled large receipts and confirm the donor PAN/name is on file. If the NPO plans a ZCZP issue on NSE-SSE (e-IPO from INR 10,000), all 80G receipts MUST be fully traced — the e-IPO facility creates a donor audit trail that makes anonymous treatment untenable.
